title: The Boy and the Nettles
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Boy was gathering berries from a hedge when his hand was stung by a Nettle. Smarting with the pain, he ran to tell his mother, and said to her between his sobs, "I only touched it ever so lightly, mother." "That's just why you got stung, my son," she said; "if you had grasped it firmly, it wouldn't have hurt you in the least."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Boy doing when his hand was stung?
options: Gathering berries from a hedge
Climbing a tree
Chasing a butterfly
Picking flowers in a field

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what stung the Boy's hand?
options: A bee
A Nettle
A thorn
A wasp

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Boy do after he was stung?
options: He ran to tell his mother
He pulled up the whole hedge
He hid the injury from his mother
He ran to find a doctor

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Boy tell his mother about how he touched the Nettle?
options: That he grasped it as hard as he could
That he only touched it ever so lightly
That he stepped on it by accident
That another boy pushed his hand into it

questions.prompt: According to the mother, what would have kept the Boy from being hurt at all?
options: Wearing gloves before touching the hedge
Grasping the Nettle firmly
Avoiding the hedge entirely
Asking her for help first

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "smarting" mean in "smarting with the pain"?
options: Feeling sharp, stinging pain
Feeling proud and clever
Feeling sleepy
Feeling hungry

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the mother say a light touch caused more pain than a firm grasp would have?
options: A light touch was actually the correct way to handle the Nettle
Facing a difficulty half-heartedly can cause more harm than confronting it boldly
The Nettle only stings when it is touched more than once
The Boy's hand was more sensitive than most people's

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Berries are not worth the risk of gathering them from a hedge
Facing a difficulty boldly can hurt less than approaching it timidly
Mothers always know better than their children
Nettles should be removed from every hedge

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Boy speak to his mother about what happened?
options: Between his sobs
In a calm, steady voice
While laughing
In a whisper

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the mother call the Boy when she answers him?
options: "My son"
"My dear"
"Silly boy"
"My little berry-picker"

questions.prompt: According to the mother, what is the exact reason the Boy got stung?
options: He touched the Nettle too lightly
He touched the Nettle too many times
He touched the Nettle in the wrong season
He touched a different plant by mistake

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "grasped" mean in "if you had grasped it firmly"?
options: Avoided
Held tightly
Watched closely
Cut off

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what lesson might the Boy take from his mother's explanation?
options: He should give hedges a wide berth from now on
He should confront difficult or risky things with confidence rather than hesitation
He should always ask an adult before touching any plant
He should stop gathering berries altogether

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Boy is stung by a Nettle, and his mother explains that a light touch, not a firm one, was the real cause of his pain
A Boy's mother forbids him from ever gathering berries again
A Boy is stung by a Nettle and his mother scolds him for going near the hedge
A Boy learns to grasp nettles lightly to avoid being stung
